extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal professionals involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order describing the standards, statutory/regulatory basis, stipulated facts, findings, and agreed sanctions in a USPTO disciplinary proceeding against a registered patent attorney. Covers which rules apply, the triggering facts (public state discipline), misconduct characterization, and imposed remedies/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent attorneys are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'Respondent ... is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.' This establishes that practitioners registered to practice before the Office are governed by those regulations for professional conduct and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director jurisdiction for disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites statutory and regulatory bases for USPTO jurisdiction and discipline, indicating the procedural authority under which the Office may approve settlement agreements and issue Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public state discipline as a ground for USPTO discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Joint Legal Conclusion states Respondent 'acknowledges that ... Respondent's acts and omissions violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) by being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.' This identifies prior public discipline by a state authority as a trigger for USPTO disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (Colorado Rule 8.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Colorado Rule of Professional Conduct 8.4(c) prohibits conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation; violating a duty of candor can constitute such misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Stipulation provides that Respondent 'violated his duty of candor' to Wells Fargo by not informing the bank that the accounts were opened on behalf of marijuana dispensaries, and 'as a result, Respondent stipulated that he violated Colorado Rule of Professional Conduct 8.4(c).' This exemplifies that failure to disclose material facts to third parties (here, the bank) can be characterized as dishonesty/misrepresentation for discipline purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to be candid with third parties and to respect third-party policies
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney's arrangement of client trust accounts and conduct concerning those accounts must respect third-party (e.g., bank) policies and duties of candor; knowingly omitting material information to a third party can be misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulated facts: Respondent arranged for two client trust accounts at Wells Fargo, was aware Wells Fargo did not permit marijuana-related businesses to maintain accounts, and did not inform the bank of the accounts' purpose. The Order uses this as the factual basis for the state sanction and the USPTO finding. The example signals that arranging financial accounts while concealing the client's business type from the financial institution is an anti-pattern and disciplinary risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: public censure
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreed upon sanction in this matter is that the Respondent is publicly censured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'Respondent is publicly censured.' The Order also prescribes publication steps (see separate metric) and notes the censure resolves the disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts as part of the settlement agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements for disciplinary Final Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires electronic publication at https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/ and prescribes an Official Gazette notice that summarizes the disciplinary finding and the factual basis (the example notice text is included verbatim in the Order). This establishes transparency and public notice practices for disciplinary resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct, and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly preserves the Office's ability to rely on the record as (1) material in addressing new complaints of similar conduct and (2) an aggravating factor or rebuttal tool in future discipline. Practitioners should understand that settlements and published orders may be used against them later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of reconsideration, review, and appeal rights as settlement term
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the settlement, the Respondent waives seeking reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, review under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and otherwise appealing or challenging the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists these waivers as part of the agreed-upon sanctions, indicating common settlement provisions that conclude administrative review rights in exchange for an agreed resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides that each side bears its own costs as part of the settlement, signaling that cost allocation is an explicit term that may be negotiated in disciplinary settlements.
